$comment: Shading bake for the real-tissue look (tools/bake-shading.mjs). occluders: which layers can shade each layer. Each layer shades only itself and the parts that never move apart from it (discs with vertebrae, teeth with the skull, knee ligaments with the leg), so posing never leaves shadows where a bone used to be. The muscles are baked in their rest shape; each region shades only itself, as muscles of different regions slide over each other when posed.

tendon.$comment: Tendon mask in _TISSUE.a. minBelly: muscles whose belly (85th percentile thickness) is thinner than this get no thickness-based tendon; thin: tendon below thin[0] × belly, fading out by thin[1] × belly; maxThickness: never tendon above this (m); outer: only outside the middle of the muscle along its long axis (distance from the middle, as a share of its length); rules add aponeuroses by node name.

rules.$comment: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea) between the bellies, 1 mm thick (tools/refine-muscles.mjs).

The aponeuroses of the abdominal wall: the obliques and transversus turn into aponeurosis medially (the rectus sheath, meeting at the linea alba) and below the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus. border: [height y, distance from the midline |x|] in metres.
The thoracolumbar fascia: latissimus dorsi arises by a broad aponeurosis from the lumbar spines and the iliac crest.
The abdominal part of pectoralis major arises by a short aponeurosis from the front of the rectus sheath; its lowest tip shows on the sheath.
The three tendinous intersections: at the umbilicus, at the xiphoid and midway (share of the muscle's height from the pubis).
